name: IL-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Miller with large financial edge
Minimal Democratic fundraising and no polling
model.rationale: The R+20 district, incumbent Miller's $810k war chest against Todd's $34k, and prediction markets at 96% Republican all point to a safe Republican hold, with only the favorable Democratic environment tempering the margin slightly.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the incumbent under 60% or a surge of outside spending against Miller would warrant reclassification.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This heavily Republican southern Illinois district sits about 20 points to the right of the nation, and incumbent Mary Miller is seeking another term after easily securing renomination. She has raised over $1.3 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Democrat Jennifer Todd has raised little more than $100,000 with modest reserves. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, but prediction markets give Miller roughly a 96% chance of winning.

The Democratic environment nationally is favorable, which could trim Miller's margin somewhat, but with no polling, minimal outside spending, and a steep partisan baseline, the race remains firmly in Republican hands. The realistic question is the size of Miller's victory, not the outcome.
